moments.title: Jensen's glass haystack opens
moments.text: Landscape architect Jens Jensen replaced three small Victorian greenhouses in Garfield, Douglas and Humboldt parks with one big conservatory, shaped to suggest a Midwestern haystack. Inside, plants grew in naturalistic landscapes, with stone walls hiding the machinery.

moments.title: A hailstorm shatters the roof
moments.text: Hail broke an estimated half or more of the glass, from about 23,000 to 31,000 panes by different counts. Rooms with newer laminated glass held up and reopened within days.

moments.title: The Fern Room reopens
moments.text: The conservatory's historic Fern Room reopened after repairs, while other houses stayed closed.

moments.title: Fully reopened
moments.text: With about 31,000 hand-cut panes of stronger laminated glass replaced, the whole conservatory reopened. Reported costs range from $5.4 million to $15 million.

moments.title: Today: Garfield Park Conservatory
moments.text: The conservatory at 300 N. Central Park Ave covers about 4.5 acres and is one of the largest in the country.

sources.title: Garfield Park Conservatory (The Cultural Landscape Foundation)

checked.notes: Opened 1908 (Chicago Park District, Archipedia), Jensen design consolidating three greenhouses, haystack form (Park District, TCLF). 4.5 acres (Wikipedia). June 30, 2011 hailstorm; broken-glass estimates 50 to 70 percent; Fern Room reopened Dec 2011; full reopening Apr 2015 with 31,000 panes; cost $5.4 million (AP) or $15 million (Hartley). Story confirmed; no changes.
